property_summary: For any inputs to initialize(...), the reference contract sets baseToken to the provided _baseToken (i.e. c.baseToken() == _baseToken after initialize returns); the mutant instead sometimes sets baseToken to msg.sender, breaking this equality for some fuzzed inputs.

For any initialize(...) call the reference contract sets its public baseToken to the provided _baseToken argument; the mutant always sets baseToken to address(0) so there exist inputs where c.baseToken() != _baseToken and the property is violated.

For any input parameters to initialize, the deployed contract's public baseToken equals the _baseToken argument passed to initialize; the mutant sets baseToken to the factory address instead and thus can make baseToken != _baseToken for some inputs.

For any inputs to initialize, the deployed pool's public nft getter equals the _nft argument passed to initialize (reference preserves stored nft), whereas the mutant sets nft to address(0) and thus violates this for some inputs.
After initialize(...) completes, the nft getter must equal the _nft argument passed (i.e. c.nft() == _nft); the mutant assigns nft = _baseToken so for some fuzzed inputs this invariant is violated.

For every call to initialize(..., _nft, ...), the reference contract stores nft == _nft (its public getter returns the same address passed in); the mutant sets nft to the factory address instead, so for some fuzzed _nft values the stored nft will differ and the property is violated.

For any inputs to initialize the contract's nft state variable is set exactly to the provided _nft address (even if zero) in the reference; the mutant sets nft to address(this) when _nft == address(0), violating that rule for some inputs where _nft == address(0).

For every initialize(...) call the reference stores nft == _nft (the provided address); the mutant sets nft == address(this) when _nft == address(0), so there exist inputs (_nft == address(0)) where nft != _nft and the property is violated.

For any call to initialize(...), the reference contract sets nft() equal to the address passed as the _nft parameter; the mutant sets nft() to address(this) when _nft == address(0), so there exist inputs with _nft == address(0) that make nft() != _nft (i.e. the stored nft differs from the supplied parameter).

For every call to initialize(...), the reference contract accepts any _nft value (including address(0)) and stores exactly that value in nft(); the mutant instead maps an input _nft == address(0) to nft() == address(this), so there exist fuzzed inputs (where _nft == address(0)) for which nft() != _nft and the property is violated.

For every initialize(...) call the reference stores nft() equal to the raw _nft parameter passed in; the mutant maps a zero _nft to address(this) so there exist inputs (_nft == address(0)) for which nft() != _nft and the property is violated.

For every input to initialize(..., _changeFee, ...), the reference contract stores changeFee equal to the exact _changeFee passed in (c.changeFee() == _changeFee); the mutant stores a shifted value so for some fuzzed _changeFee the stored value differs, violating this rule.
For any initialize(...) call, the contract's public changeFee equals the exact _changeFee parameter passed; the mutant that writes _changeFee + 1 will violate this (for many non-maximal inputs).
For any inputs to initialize, the contract's stored changeFee equals the provided _changeFee (reference); the mutant that always sets changeFee to 0 will violate this when _changeFee != 0.

For every admissible feeRate input (uint16), calling initialize(...) on a fresh C either sets feeRate to the provided value but only if it's <= 5000 (reference always enforces the 5000 cap), whereas the mutant allows larger feeRate values so there exist inputs (feeRate > 5000) where C.feeRate() in the mutant differs from the reference; the reference never accepts feeRate > 5000, but the mutant does.
For any initialize(...) call that succeeds, the contract's public feeRate equals the _feeRate parameter passed in; the mutant breaks this by forcing feeRate to zero regardless of the input _feeRate.

For any admissible _feeRate (0..5000) passed to initialize, the reference contract stores feeRate equal to the provided _feeRate; the mutant instead stores feeRate = ~_feeRate (bitwise NOT), so there exist inputs where stored feeRate differs.
